IR.rationale: A steepening curve signals improving growth and reflation expectations, which raise expected demand for industrial commodities and support their prices.

B.rationale: Strong high-yield returns with stable Baa spreads describe easy, risk-on credit conditions. Such conditions accompany cyclical demand and investor inflows into commodities.

V.rationale: Elevated commodity-specific implied volatility marks periods when hedging pressure and the risk premium paid to speculators are high, which predicts subsequent futures returns.

AP.rationale: Emerging-market equity strength proxies for EM growth, the marginal driver of commodity demand, and it tends to lead commodity prices.

ST.rationale: Equity cross-sectional style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to commodity futures returns, so this group is left empty.

FX.rationale: A weakening broad dollar together with a strong commodity currency reflects global reflation. Commodity currencies also have documented predictive power for commodity prices.

COM.rationale: Time-series momentum in commodity futures is well documented: recent broad commodity strength tends to persist over weeks to months.

MC.rationale: Rising breakeven inflation under loose financial conditions captures an inflationary, risk-tolerant environment in which commodities act as inflation hedges and attract inflows.

ENDG.rationale: The index's own recent return captures own-asset time-series momentum, documented across commodity markets.

IR.rationale: A jump in the 1-year rate relative to Fed Funds signals a repricing of the monetary policy path. Such repricings tighten dollar funding and raise volatility across risk assets, including commodities.

B.rationale: Widening Baa spreads alongside weak high-yield returns identify emerging credit stress, which precedes deleveraging and higher commodity volatility.

V.rationale: Commodity implied volatilities embed forward-looking information on future realised variance beyond what past realised variance contains. Joint elevation in oil and gold implied volatility signals broad commodity turbulence.

AP.rationale: Equity sell-offs raise risk aversion and trigger cross-asset deleveraging. Through this leverage and volatility-feedback channel they predict higher subsequent volatility, including in financialized commodities.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors offer no clear mechanism for commodity variance beyond what market and volatility variables already capture.

FX.rationale: Sharp dollar appreciation tightens global financial conditions and reprices dollar-denominated commodities, which is associated with higher commodity volatility.

COM.rationale: Falling commodity prices are linked to forced liquidation and inventory adjustments, which tend to raise subsequent realised volatility.

MC.rationale: Elevated systemic financial stress predicts higher volatility across asset classes because liquidity deteriorates and risk-bearing capacity shrinks.

ENDG.rationale: Unusually high recent realised variance relative to its own history captures volatility clustering and the speed at which it mean-reverts.

IR.rationale: Curve flattening signals tightening and weakening growth expectations, conditions under which cyclical commodity demand disappoints.

B.rationale: Widening corporate spreads combined with weak EM sovereign bonds describe global risk-off with EM stress, which is the typical backdrop for sharp commodity sell-offs.

V.rationale: High commodity and equity implied volatility together signal fat left tails and correlated deleveraging across asset classes.

AP.rationale: Weak emerging-market equities signal deteriorating demand from the main source of commodity consumption growth.

ST.rationale: Style factors have no established link to commodity downside tails, so this group is left empty.

FX.rationale: A strengthening dollar together with weak commodity currencies is the classic configuration preceding commodity price slumps.

COM.rationale: Through momentum and liquidation dynamics, recent broad commodity weakness raises the chance of further large declines.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions with falling inflation expectations identify a deflationary, risk-off regime in which commodities suffer large losses.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent own returns capture downside momentum and selling pressure that make further tail losses more likely.

IR.rationale: Steepening reflects reflationary growth expectations that can drive strong commodity rallies.

B.rationale: Strong high-yield and EM sovereign bond returns indicate global risk appetite and easing EM funding, which support sharp commodity upswings.

V.rationale: Commodity-specific uncertainty with calm equity markets points to supply-driven or idiosyncratic shocks, which can produce large commodity gains rather than broad risk-off losses.

AP.rationale: Strong EM equities signal accelerating demand from commodity-intensive economies.

ST.rationale: Style factors carry no clear information on commodity upside tails, so this group is left empty.

FX.rationale: A falling dollar together with strong commodity currencies is the typical configuration accompanying commodity rallies.

COM.rationale: Commodity time-series momentum makes recent broad strength informative about further large gains.

MC.rationale: Rising inflation expectations coincide with inflation-hedging demand and reflationary episodes that generate large commodity gains.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent own returns reflect upside momentum that raises the chance of an upper-tail outcome.
